modification_description: Disclosure of uncertainty should be individualized based on patient preferences and clinical risk level, rather than applied as a one-size-fits-all approach. Specifically: (1) assess or ask the patient how much detail they want upfront; (2) structure uncertainty communication to convey what is most likely, what is uncertain, and what will resolve it—avoiding speculative open-ended differentials presented as equally likely; (3) make the follow-up plan concrete with timing for tests, review points, and escalation triggers so the patient does not carry the burden of uncertainty alone.
